chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū Makhlad al-Sarrāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a man who called another man ‘son of the madman,’ and the other said, ‘You are the son of the madman.’ So he ordered the first one to lash his companion twenty lashes, and said to him, ‘Know that it will be followed by twenty like it.’ Then when he had lashed him, they gave the whip to the one who had been lashed, and he lashed him as a deterrent by which both of them were punished.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in his capacity as judge and leader
key_terms.ابْنَ الْمَجْنُونِ: an insulting attribution meaning son of the madman
key_terms.السَّوْطَ: the whip used for the lashing
key_terms.عِشْرِينَ جَلْدَةً: twenty lashes as the prescribed disciplinary punishment in this case
key_terms.قَضَى: gave judgment; issued a legal ruling
key_terms.نَكَالًا: as a deterrent and exemplary punishment
key_terms.يَجْلِدَ: to lash; to administer corporal punishment
key_terms.يُنَكِّلُ بِهِمَا: serving to punish and deter both of them

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام on two men who insulted each other by saying ‘son of the madman’?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning mutual insult and retaliatory verbal abuse. It shows a measured disciplinary punishment intended to deter both parties from engaging in defamatory or abusive speech.
